extra.message: User-controlled "host" parameter is concatenated directly into a shell command via os.system(). An attacker can inject arbitrary commands using shell metacharacters such as ;, |, or $(...) to achieve remote code execution.

User-controlled "fragment" parameter is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 template string and rendered. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI). An attacker can inject Jinja2 expressions like {{config}} or {{''.__class__.__mro__[2].__subclasses__()}} to achieve remote code execution.

User-controlled JSON payload is passed directly to MongoDB find_one() as a filter query. An attacker can inject MongoDB operators like {$ne}, {$regex}, {$gt} to bypass authentication or extract unauthorized data.

The SPA catch-all route resolves user-controlled URL path segments against the frontend_dist directory without sanitization. An attacker can traverse directories (e.g. ../../../etc/passwd) to read arbitrary files on the server via FileResponse.

User-controlled "ref" parameter (from query params or JSON body) is concatenated into a file path without sanitization. An attacker can use ../ sequences to write JSON files containing SSN and credit card data to arbitrary locations on the filesystem.
User-controlled "name" parameter is used directly as a file path without sanitization. An attacker can use ../ sequences to write arbitrary binary content to any location on the filesystem.

User-controlled "copyline" query parameter is concatenated directly into HTML without any escaping or sanitization. An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML and JavaScript via the copyline parameter, leading to reflected Cross-Site Scripting.

User-controlled "card" parameter is rendered in a Jinja2 template with the |safe filter, which explicitly disables HTML escaping. An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML and JavaScript via the card parameter, leading to Cross-Site Scripting.
User-controlled "lane" query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse() without validation. An attacker can redirect users to arbitrary external URLs, enabling phishing attacks.
The full Authorization header (bearer token) is logged to application logs. This exposes session tokens or API keys in log files, which may be accessible to unauthorized parties.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Hardcoded default SSN (111-22-3333) and credit card number (4111111111111111) are written to the filesystem in JSON format. These default values represent sensitive PII stored insecurely and exposed via the API.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The response returns sensitive internal fields: sync_key (an API key), tax_ref (a tax ID), and ops_memo (internal operational notes). This exposes confidential operational data to any caller with the gate token.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is set to the attacker-controlled Origin request header, and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to true. This allows any external website to make credentialed cross-origin requests, enabling CSRF-style attacks against authenticated endpoints.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: X-XSS-Protection is explicitly set to 0 (disabling browser XSS filters) and Content-Security-Policy is set to an empty string (disabling CSP). This weakens browser-side security protections.

User-controlled JSON body is merged into the workset dict via .update() without restricting which keys can be overridden. An attacker can set is_admin: true or role: admin to escalate privileges, or modify credit_limit to bypass financial controls.
MD5 is used for hashing user-controlled input. MD5 is cryptographically broken and vulnerable to collision attacks. This should be replaced with SHA-256 or stronger.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: random.choice() is used to generate a nonce-like value. The random module uses Mersenne Twister, which is predictable. Use secrets.choice() for cryptographically secure randomness.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: A hardcoded default secret key dev-only-change-me-support-desk is used when the SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set. This weak default secret key could allow attackers to forge session tokens if not overridden in production.
